MZ5 landed the Linux RCL backend via a system ROS 2 install (ament prefix, not an xcframework): .zenoh -> rcl+rmw_zenoh_cpp and .dds/.rcl -> rcl+rmw_cyclonedds_cpp, with the rmw selected per-process at runtime via RMW_IMPLEMENTATION. Verified on Ubuntu 24.04 / ROS 2 Jazzy: crcl-loopback 20/20 in-process over cyclonedds; talker->listener 10/10 over a live rmw_zenohd router; SwiftROS2RCLTests green in the ci-rcl Linux leg. One process serves .zenoh OR .dds (the rmw is process-global) — switching transports needs separate processes. Latency + correctness axes measured 2026-07-11 on youtalk-desktop (see axis cells) after the #164 routing fix — the earlier MZ5 verification exercised .rcl configs and crcl-loopback below the public API, which is how the .dds ROS2Context regression slipped through. rcl=partial: the transport layer is now verified end-to-end on both rmws; the full per-type/service/action Linux capability matrix is not yet individually run. |
